prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

S150: Work Permit Portal is referred to as Redoubt in this section.
S151: The authorization lifecycle begins when a work request is entered with its location, scope, planned duration, and responsible team.
S152: The requester identifies the equipment affected and describes the intended work in terms that can be checked against operating constraints.
S153: Duty Planner reviews the request for completeness and assigns it to the appropriate planning queue.
S154: Maintenance Planning Engine can use reviewed condition information when prioritizing future maintenance activities.
S155: Work Permit Portal maintains the request record and its revision history throughout review and execution.

S157: HSE Officer reviews the proposed controls when the task presents a material personnel or environmental risk.
S158: Technical reviewers confirm that the work scope is compatible with equipment condition and the planned maintenance method.
S159: SCADA Gateway uses the deviation notice to flag work packages that may require technical review.
S160: Marine Coordinator checks that the planned access method and timing are practical for the work location.
S161: Vessel Master confirms that the vessel plan can support the approved personnel and equipment transfer.
S162: Work Permit Portal records review decisions and returns incomplete requests to the requester with the required corrections identified.
S163: Warehouse System produces a Backorder Exception Slip when a requested component cannot be supplied by the planned issue date.

S170: The responsible team reports completion status and outstanding issues before the permit is closed.
S171: Juniper Vale shall provide current operational status to permit reviewers when requested as part of the authorization check.
S172: Closed records remain available for audit, incident review, and future planning.
S173: During normal operation, station service transformers at the Offshore Substation supply the facility's auxiliary electrical loads from the medium-voltage collection system.
S174: The normal supply serves control systems, lighting, ventilation, communications, and equipment required for safe switching and maintenance.
S175: Essential loads are separated from nonessential loads so that backup capacity can be reserved for safety and control functions.
S176: The Emergency Generator is assigned the operational alias Foxglove for maintenance and alarm references.
S177: On loss of the normal auxiliary supply, automatic controls initiate the Emergency Generator start sequence.
S178: Transfer to the emergency bus occurs only after voltage and frequency are within the configured acceptance limits.
S179: The transfer arrangement prevents the normal and emergency sources from being connected in parallel unless an approved synchronizing function is provided.
S180: The Emergency Generator supplies the designated emergency distribution bus and is not intended to support turbine export production.
S181: Loads connected to the emergency distribution bus are prioritized according to their contribution to personnel safety, equipment protection, and controlled shutdown.
S182: Nonessential loads are shed automatically when generator capacity is insufficient or the measured load exceeds its operating limit.
S183: If the Emergency Generator does not start or stabilize, the system raises an alarm and maintains any available uninterruptible control power.
S184: Operators use the approved recovery procedure to assess the fault, preserve essential services, and restore the normal supply when it is safe to do so.
S185: The Electrical Technician verifies protective device settings and transfer interlocks during planned maintenance.
S186: Scheduled exercising confirms that the Emergency Generator can start, accept its expected load, and operate for the required test duration.
S187: Fuel condition, cooling, lubrication, battery readiness, and exhaust ventilation are checked as part of the generator readiness program.
S188: Maintenance Planning Engine schedules inspections and corrective work using equipment condition and operating history.
S189: Morrowick maintains the designated emergency distribution bus within its approved operating limits.
S190: The Grid Interface Relay provides status indications that support assessment of the normal supply and its protective state.
S191: The Turbine Controller enters its configured safe operating mode when required auxiliary services are unavailable.
S192: The SCADA Gateway presents supply alarms and generator status to the Shore Control Room for remote awareness.
S193: The Control Engineer reviews persistent alarms and coordinates electrical support with the Substation Operator.
S194: Metocean Buoy produces the Wave Burst Record at the configured sampling interval.
S195: Thistle Crown schedules periodic reviews of standby electrical maintenance requirements and outstanding corrective work.
